HelpAfs: Adaptive Flow Scale is part of Adaptive Motion Learning. From what the study measured - how far this game's picture moves from one frame to the next - it picks Flow for the game by itself: finer for slow games (75%), lighter and steadier for fast ones (35%), 50% between. Once the game is learned it replaces Game type and Flow. Turn it off to set them yourself.
WhatIsAml: Learns how your mouse, keyboard and controller move the picture in each game, so the generated frames follow your movements better. The first time, follow the short steps shown at the top of the screen.
WhatIsAfs: Picks the Flow size for each game by itself: finer for slow games, lighter for fast ones. It works with Adaptive Motion Learning.
CacheEmpty: Nothing saved yet. Turn it on under Game type and play.
PresetCWarning: Not recommended. Preset C lowers the image quality a lot, and the performance you gain from it is small.
GameFpsHelp: The game's own frame rate. On Auto the app reads it from the frames; type your game's rate (20 to 500) if the frame rate shown jumps around with what you do in the game. Empty is Auto.
FeedbackHint: What happened? What would you like to see? (in any language)
FeedbackNoLog: No log yet: turn on “Keep a log” in Settings and play once.
FeedbackWait: Please wait a little before sending again.
FeedbackWhat: Only your message, the app's and Windows' versions and, if ticked, the log are sent - and only when you press Send.
VideoIntro: Make your videos smoother with frames made in between, and larger or sharper if you like. Add videos, choose each one's settings, then press Start: they are done one after the other.
VideoEmpty: No videos yet. Press "Add videos" to choose one or more.
VideoStopped: Stopped - the part made so far is saved
VideoStopMotionFirst: Stop Super Motion first: both use the graphics card.
VideoNote: Videos are made with SMFG, on any card. DLSS MFG and XeSS MFG make frames only on the live screen (Super Motion). Sound is kept.
SmfgAiHelp: Experimental. The frames in between are made by a neural network on your card's AI units (NVIDIA tensor cores, AMD AI accelerators, Intel XMX) - fewer pieces coming apart in fast movement and on thin things. Heavier than SMFG: about 10 ms of an RTX 3060 for each pair at x2 (SMFG: under 2), so it is for strong cards and x2 or x3. Super Video can use it on any card.
AdaptiveHelp: Frames shown a second, at an even pace (starts at the screen's refresh).
MultiDisplayHelp: The picture stays while you use a window on another screen (the game no longer has to be in front).
CropHelp: Pixels left out of the game's window on each side (black bars, a frame).
CursorScaledOnly: When the picture is scaled onto the screen.
StudyTurn: Stand still. Move the camera left and right.
StudyLook: Now move the camera up and down.

HelpStart:
1. Run the game in borderless or windowed mode.
2. Choose a generator and a mode (×2 to ×6).
3. Press START MOTION, then switch to the game before the countdown ends.
4. Use the shortcut (Shift + Alt + M unless you changed it) to start and stop while you play.

If the graphics card is already at 100%, limit the game's own frame rate a little: making frames needs some room.
HelpDlss: NVIDIA's frame generation. Needs an NVIDIA RTX graphics card.
HelpXess: Intel's frame generation. It runs on many graphics cards, not all: if yours cannot run it, the app tells you.
HelpMsm: Our own generator. It works on any graphics card and is the lightest of the three. Under Advanced, “SMFG · Fast” is the lightest; “SMFG” looks for the motion more carefully.
HelpMode: Fixed: the Multiplier sets how many frames are shown for each frame of the game (×2 doubles the frame rate, ×6 shows six). Adaptive: frames are shown at an even pace of the Target (empty: the screen's refresh) whatever the game draws, as in Lossless Scaling.
HelpGameType: Tells the engine what kind of picture to expect. “Custom” opens Flow: the share of the picture the motion is worked out at — lower is lighter, higher is finer.
HelpAml: Learns, for each game, how your mouse, keys and gamepad move the picture, how late the game follows, and where its HUD is. The first time, a short study appears at the top of the screen: follow its steps (move the camera, walk forward, then play freely for 30 seconds). Performance is a little lower while it learns and improves when it is done. Only how far the mouse and sticks move and which buttons are held is counted — never what you type. What is learned is kept per game (Settings → Cache) and helps SMFG follow fast turns and keep the HUD steady. It hears every gamepad: Xbox, DualSense, DualShock, Switch Pro and others. It also learns what your buttons do: the run button (the picture moves faster) and the aim button (the camera turns slower), used the moment you press them. Adaptive Flow Scale (part of it, can be turned off): Flow is chosen for each game from how fast its picture moves, finer for slow games and lighter and steadier for fast ones; it replaces Game type and Flow once the game is learned.
HelpUpscaling: “Sharpness only” sharpens the picture. Integer, Nearest Neighbor and Anime4K enlarge a game that runs below the screen's resolution — for pixel art, retro games and anime.
HelpStill: The HUD, the crosshair and on-screen text stay as sharp and steady as the game drew them.
HelpPacing: Queue target: lower gives less delay, higher gives smoother motion. Low latency keeps the delay small. Frame limit caps the frames shown; “Limit to refresh rate” never makes more frames than the screen can show.
HelpScreen: VRR: for a G-SYNC or FreeSync screen — each frame is shown the moment it is ready. Sync mode: tearing allowed, the default pacing, or VSync. HDR: turn it on when the game itself is shown in HDR.
HelpMotion: How the movement between two frames is found. Each generator has its own choices; the default is the best starting point.
HelpCapture: Capture API: how the game's picture is taken — change it only if the output is black or stutters. Game window: Borderless is best; “Scaled to screen” stretches a smaller window. Countdown: the time you have to switch to the game.
HelpGpu: Preferred GPU: the card that makes the frames. With two cards, the second can make them so the game keeps the first for itself. GPU priority “Realtime” lets the frames go first.
HelpCounter: Shows the game's own frame rate and the frame rate you see, in a corner of the picture.
HelpObs:
Screen recorders capture the game without the generated frames. To record what you actually see:
1. Install OBS Studio and the OBS Spout2 plugin (links below).
2. Here, open Advanced → Capture and turn on “Spout output (OBS)”.
3. Press START MOTION and switch to your game.
4. In OBS: Sources → + → Spout2 Capture, and choose the sender “MFG SUPER MOTION”.
5. In OBS → Settings → Video, set the FPS you want to record (60 or 120, for example).
HelpTrouble:
Black or frozen picture: use borderless mode, or try another Capture API.
Stutter or a low frame rate: choose a lower mode, “SMFG · Fast”, or limit the game's frame rate.
The engine writes what it does to %LOCALAPPDATA%\MFG SUPER MOTION\Engine\engine.log — send that file when you report a problem.
StudyDrive: Now drive a car. No car? Just stand still.
StudyNotice: Learning costs a little performance. It gets better when done.
StudyHud: Keep moving. Switch weapons or items a few times.
StudyRun: Now run: hold your run button while you move.
StudyAim: Now aim: hold your aim button and move the camera.
StudyFree: Now play as you like for 30 seconds.
